newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: No sign Singaporeans avoiding Australia - minister.
newsitem.headline: No sign Singaporeans avoiding Australia - minister.

text.p: Singapore's foreign minister said on Monday there was no sign Singaporeans were avoiding Australia in significant numbers despite recent reports of assault on them.
S. Jayakumar told parliament there was no proof of a systematic campaign directed against Singapore citizens.
"There is no indication of Singaporeans avoiding Australia for holidays, study or business in significant numbers," Jayakumar said in response to queries by two members of parliament (MP).
"Our High Commission in Canberra has assessed that these were isolated incidents...There is no evidence of a systematic campaign being directed only at Singaporeans," he added.
In October, a Queensland town mayor Barbara Wildin said recent attacks against Singapore soldiers stemmed from anti-Asian immigration sentiment sparked by Australian independent MP Pauline Hanson.
Hanson sparked a passionate national debate on race and immigration with a maiden parliamentary speech earlier this year warning that Australia was being swamped by Asians.
Jayakumar said there had been four incidents involving off-duty Singapore soldiers in Rockhampton, Queensland -- two cases of verbal abuse, one assault and one assault and robbery.
About 1,000 Singapore Armed Forces servicemen were in Australia in October for an exercise in the Australian Defence Forces' training area near Rockhampton.

Asked by an opposition MP whether these incidents were due to anti-Asian sentiment in Australia, Jayakumar said: "Some of the investigations are difficult because the identities of the individuals were not established.
"Since the investigations have not been concluded, it's difficult to state conclusively whether these were acts of hooliganism or were acts deliberately motivated by racial connotations," he said.

Jayakumar said his Australian counterpart had expressed regret over any racial harassment against Singaporeans and had given assurances that Canberra would take any measures necessary to protect Singaporeans and other foreigners in the country.
"We hope that Singaporeans visiting Australia will not be affected by the anti-Asian sentiments expressed by a few Australians," he said.
